demand.reason: Global gallium consumption is about 900 metric tons of primary gallium in 2025, placing it deep within the modest-demand band of 500–10,000 tons.

growth.reason: Demand is accelerating rapidly, driven by the massive expansion of GaN power semiconductors in 5G base stations, EV chargers, and AI hyperscale data centers, forcing growth rates well above 12% CAGR.

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: Gallium is a trace by-product of bauxite, so its mining follows bauxite mine output, where Guinea is the largest producer at 34% in 2025 (USGS), in the 30–50% band (Score 2). China's 99% share of primary gallium is scored under refining.


Refining: Because China dominates the upstream, non-Chinese refiners rely on Chinese feedstock or recycled scrap. China produces about 99% of the world's primary gallium (USGS), well above the 85% threshold (Score 5); its ban on gallium exports to the US was lifted for one year in November 2025.

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: Gallium resources are tied to vast global bauxite deposits. Over 100,000 tons are potentially recoverable, representing centuries of supply against current 800-ton consumption rates (>100 years).


Diversification: Gallium reserves follow bauxite reserves, which are widely spread (Guinea 26%, Australia 13%, Vietnam 11%, Indonesia 10%; HHI about 0.11), below 0.15 (Score 1), the same method used for cadmium and germanium. Recovery circuits, almost all in China, are scored under refining.

end_use.reason:
Defense & National Security (+1.5): serves as the irreplaceable component in GaAs and GaN ICs driving military radar and missile seekers. Advanced Semiconductors & Computing (+1.0): forms the absolute baseline for next-generation GaN power semiconductors. Energy Generation & Grid (+1.5): deployed in multijunction solar cells and solar inverters. Electrification & Transport (+1.0): utilized widely across EV powertrains and power management platforms. Healthcare & Biomedical (+1.0): gallium-67 is deployed in specialized medical imaging.


Sector presence scores total 6.0 across 5 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus adds +2.0, yielding an objective composite score of 8.0.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: While silicon CMOS competes in mid-tier applications, no commercially proven drop-in substitute exists at scale for high-power GaN semiconductors in defense RF arrays or high-voltage EV power electronics, requiring fundamental redesigns (Score 4).


Recyclability: Global secondary recovery focuses purely on manufacturing offcuts from GaAs wafer production. End-of-life recovery from highly dissipated micro-electronics is structurally unviable, capping total recycling within the negligible (<5%) tier.

extraction_refining.reason: Gallium extraction demands direct integration with large-scale industrial bauxite/alumina or zinc smelting operations. Concentrating gallium from Bayer process liquors through ion exchange before zone-refining it to 99.9999%+ semiconductor purity is highly complex and restricted.

upcoming_projects.reason: The project pipeline is adequate. Driven by Chinese export bans, the US is launching feasibility studies to integrate gallium recovery into domestic zinc operations, while joint-ventures tap tailings in the DRC, capable of adding 10–20% to global supply within 3–5 years.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: Despite housing a massive domestic bauxite/alumina industry, India has no operating gallium recovery circuit yet (a Heavy Water Board–BARC ion-exchange demonstration plant at NALCO's Damanjodi refinery broke ground in November 2025), rendering its semiconductor mission 100% import-dependent (Score 5).


Strategic Posture: Gallium is heavily tracked under the India Semiconductor Mission and national critical minerals list. There are no foreign equity structures or KABIL mandates, but the NALCO demonstration plant puts a concrete domestic recovery plan in motion (Score 2).

price_volatility.reason: Following China's export restrictions, gallium prices experienced extreme structural market failure, surging over 200% from ~$300/kg to peak near $1,000/kg due to weaponized supply chain bans, confirming maximum extreme volatility. USGS's import unit values rose from $277/kg in 2021 to about $580/kg in 2025; China lifted its ban on gallium exports to the US for one year in November 2025.

capability.name: Gallium
capability.next_move: Commercial gallium circuits at the big refineries, with 6N refining.
capability.what_india_has: 8.2 Mt/yr of alumina refining (~80 t/yr of gallium in the liquor at China's yield, our estimate); the NALCO-HWB/BARC ion-exchange demo plant; C-MET's 6N purification; Indian resin makers.
capability.cost: Modest: Rio Tinto's pilot and 4 t/yr demo drew C$26 m of public money; commercial scale is ~40 t/yr (#8).

strategyList.name: Gallium recovery and high-purity refining
strategyList.what: Ion-exchange resins pull gallium from Bayer liquor; electrolysis and zone refining take it to 6N-7N.
strategyList.outside_china: China ~99% of primary output; ~9 t/yr elsewhere. New: Rio Tinto (Canada) pilot and demo; Alcoa (Australia, with Japanese and US partners) has a final investment decision.
strategyList.cost: Rio Tinto: C$26 m of public support for a pilot and a demo of up to 4 t/yr; commercial scale ~40 t/yr (~5% of world output).
strategyList.india_base: NALCO-HWB/BARC demo plant (Damanjodi, Nov 2025); C-MET 6N purification; NFC; Ion Exchange India resins.

chemistryList.name: Fluorochemicals and HF
chemistryList.who: GFCL (India's largest integrated fluoropolymer maker; fluorspar mine in Morocco); Navin Fluorine (AHF project at Dahej).
chemistryList.carries_over_to: LiPF6 electrolyte salt; HF purification of graphite; rare-earth fluorides for metal making; etching chemicals for gallium and silicon devices.
chemistryList.fit: Direct for LiPF6; adjacent for the rest
chemistryList.summary: Fluorine chemistry is a shared industrial foundation for battery salts, selected mineral-purification routes and electronic chemicals. India's existing HF plants provide a starting point, but each application needs its own process, purity controls and customer qualification.

links.how: Fluoride chemistry is relevant to selected compound-semiconductor surface treatments. A GaN study removed native surface oxide using dilute HF. That supports a narrow process connection, not a claim that HF produces gallium metal or that a supplier is qualified for a commercial GaN fabrication line.

chemistryList.name: Ion-exchange resins
chemistryList.who: Ion Exchange India (Ankleshwar; hydrometallurgy and nuclear-grade resins); HWB-BARC's special resin.
chemistryList.carries_over_to: Gallium from Bayer liquor; scandium; heavy-REE polishing; lithium from brine.
chemistryList.fit: Direct for gallium (demo); adjacent for the rest
chemistryList.summary: Selective resin beads capture dissolved ions, then release them into a cleaner stream. India manufactures resins and has a gallium-recovery demonstration project, but each mineral application needs its own chemistry, feed testing and operating evidence.

links.how: The workbook’s most concrete application is selective recovery from alumina-refinery liquor. HWB’s release reports a demonstration project beginning construction, using domestic resin and solvent. It does not disclose a sustained production rate, resin lifetime or finished semiconductor-grade product output.
links.fit: Specific Indian demonstration project; operating commercial recovery unverified

chemistryList.name: High-purity and electronic materials
chemistryList.who: C-MET (6N gallium); NFC (special materials); CSIR-CGCRI (doped fibres).
chemistryList.carries_over_to: 6N-7N gallium and tellurium; Er- and Yb-doped fibres.
chemistryList.summary: Electronic and optical materials turn small quantities of very clean substances into high-value components. India has documented gallium and tellurium purification work and rare-earth-doped optical-fibre technologies. These are distinct chains: metal purity, semiconductor manufacture and fibre-device manufacture should each be assessed on their own evidence.

links.how: Builds the purification bridge between recovered or purchased gallium and electronic-material users. The demonstrated refining route does not establish domestic recovery from Bayer liquor or an entire compound-semiconductor factory.
links.fit: Direct purification capability; scale and qualification require separate evidence
